prose: The engine is headless. It runs under plain Node with no bundler, so a DOM reference typechecks clean under a shared config and then dies at runtime in the CLI.
rationale: This is why the tsconfigs are split; the invariant is the runtime half of that guarantee.

prose: The renderer reaches the Electron main process only through the preload bridge, never by importing it.
rationale: Renderer code displays agent-authored text and is treated as untrusted; a direct import would put main-process capability in its bundle.

prose: The engine is the product and the app is one consumer of it, so nothing in engine/ may reach into app/.
rationale: It has to keep running standalone as a CLI with no Electron and no React present.

prose: Unevidenced claims are rejected where they are ingested, not at review time. The guard lives in the claim store.
rationale: This is the single defence against a confabulated map; if it moves or disappears the whole design's honesty claim goes with it.

prose: The harness never passes an adapter flag that bypasses approvals or sandboxing.
rationale: Agents observe and claim; they never write code. A bypass flag would silently remove the only thing keeping that true.

prose: Nothing under engine/scene/ calls a randomness source. Position is a pure function of the focus stack, so the same repo lays out the same way every session — which is the only thing that makes flying around build spatial memory.
No symbol in the map, and no file it maps, is named after the pre-rename product. The CLI is daylight, the env prefix is DAYLIGHT_, and nothing keeps the old names alive.
rationale: The rename carries no compatibility layer (R2, R3), so an old name that survives is either dead or a fallback nobody ruled on. This is the graph half of the rule; the graph sees symbols and source files, not prose, so the full-text half (docs, strings, config, tests, with the frozen P0 records exempt) is engine/test/naming.ts in test:all.

prose: Stored transcript-derived strings are only relative paths, model names, tool names, provider ids and repo-verified shas. Nothing under engine/ingest/ calls a file-write API by name; facts are written through the mission store, the event log or the artifact store, after assertVetted has checked each string in them.
rationale: A transcript is prompts, model prose, file contents and tool output that may hold a secret (PLAN resolution 8). This is the graph half, and only a callee-name check: an aliased write or a spawned process would not trip it. The real controls are the runtime half is assertVetted at every write, and engine/test/ingest.ts, which scans all of <out> for a planted sentinel and a planted key.

prose: A candidate's verdict is computed from rows handed to it. engine/forge/verdict.ts never calls into the swarm, the mission store or the experiment runner.
rationale: ADR-19: attempt state, exit code and narrative are not verdict inputs. A verdict that could look things up could read them; this keeps the only inputs the VerdictRows its caller passes, which carry no such field. engine/test/forge-gate.ts holds the property half: the verdict is the same across attempt state, exit code and narrative.

prose: Nothing in spec intake (registering a spec, decomposing it, ingesting proposals, deciding work items) registers, starts or locks an experiment. Acceptance gates are written and locked by a person, never derived from a decomposer's proposal.
rationale: PLAN resolution 7: automating gates from a spec automates the one thing that must stay human-authored, the acceptance criterion. The row-level half (no spec mission holds an experiment, no item leaves proposed without a human decision naming its digest, no implement mission without an approved item or an adhoc-mission decision) is specIntakeViolations, tested in engine/test/spec.ts.

prose: Deciding a work item and starting an ad hoc implement mission both go through the one decision-authenticity guard, assertHumanDecision.
rationale: R10.4 and R14 D-9: one guard, owned by forge/policy.ts, wraps every decision operation; a work-item path that stopped calling it would let an agent session approve its own proposals.

prose: A sandbox gets a read-write mount only from engine/forge/sandbox.ts, where the author profile refuses it without the authorize decision that granted the attempt write, and the exec sandbox refuses it unless the attempt row holds exec over that grant.
rationale: R7: write is a mode, granted only by a human authorize-mission decision and stamped on the attempt. A second place that emits bwrap's --bind would be a write path that never asks; the store refuses the row (unauthorizedWriteAttempts), this keeps the mount honest to it. The graph sees call arguments, so a --bind spelled inside an array literal is not caught here; engine/test/forge-sandbox.ts asserts the mount lists themselves.

prose: The project ledger and its report take every dollar and token figure from attempt rows; neither reads the event log.
rationale: Events narrate spend more than once: a merged usage line, provider.cost and the capture's cost.reported all describe the same dollars, so a sum over them double-counts. The attempt row is the ledger of record (PLAN F-9). The runtime half (null never summed as zero, scanned never known, no cost on a none row) is engine/test/ledger.ts and the attempt_usage CHECKs.

prose: No symbol in the ledger, report, usage, capture or normalize modules is a price, rate or per-token table, used or not. Dollars come only from what a provider reported; tokens never become dollars.
rationale: An estimated figure printed beside reported ones is the fabrication the ledger exists to prevent, and an unused table is one call away from being used. This matches any symbol by name, reachable or not; engine/test/ledger.ts scans the same files' source for the shape of a rate whatever it is called.

prose: engine/forge/decide.ts calls WS1's assertHumanDecision, the one R13 guard, for approve, reject and override.
rationale: R10.4 and R14 D-9: every candidate act goes through one guard, never a reimplementation. engine/test/forge-apply.ts holds the behavioural half: CLAUDECODE, DAYLIGHT_SESSION, an agent actor and a wrong --confirm are each refused.

prose: engine/forge/apply.ts calls WS1's assertHumanDecision, the one R13 guard, before it writes anything to a repository.
rationale: R10.4 and resolution 13 name apply as a guarded act. engine/test/forge-apply.ts holds the behavioural half: apply under CLAUDECODE or with another act's code is refused and makes no ref.
